findings.title: ERC-7201 Storage Location Constants Unverified
findings.cwe: CWE-710: Improper Adherence to Coding Standards
findings.description: Hardcoded ERC-7201 storage location constants claim to be derived from keccak256(abi.encode(uint256(keccak256(namespace)) - 1)) & ~bytes32(uint256(0xff)), but values appear suspiciously 'clean' for cryptographic hashes. No on-chain verification or test coverage exists to confirm correct calculation.
findings.exploit_sketch: Incorrect storage location calculation could cause storage collision or corruption during upgrades, leading to complete protocol state loss.
findings.impact: Protocol bricked on upgrade - all state lost
findings.mitigation: Add test to verify storage locations match ERC-7201 calculation: assertEq(calculated_location, hardcoded_constant);

findings.title: No Timelock on UUPS Upgrades
findings.cwe: CWE-349: Acceptance of Extraneous Untrusted Data With Trusted Data
findings.description: UUPS upgrade authorization requires only DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE with no timelock delay. Compromised admin key enables instant protocol takeover, fund drain, or bricking.
findings.exploit_sketch:
1. Admin key compromised
2. Attacker immediately upgrades to malicious implementation
3. Drain all funds or brick protocol
4. No time for community response or fund recovery
findings.impact: Instant total protocol takeover, fund loss, or bricking
findings.mitigation: Deploy behind TimelockController with 48h minimum delay on upgrades

findings.title: No Timelock on Critical Parameter Changes
findings.description: Critical protocol parameters (fees, bonds, stake requirements) can be changed instantly by admin without timelock. Enables economic attacks or protocol manipulation.
findings.exploit_sketch:
1. Admin sets protocol fees to 100% (10,000 bps)
2. All future operations extract maximum fees
3. Users lose all rewards, protocol becomes unusable
findings.impact: Economic attack via parameter manipulation, protocol becomes unprofitable

findings.title: Storage Layout Compatibility Not Tested
findings.cwe: CWE-710: Improper Adherence to Coding Standards
findings.description: No tests verify storage layout compatibility across upgrades. Future upgrades could accidentally modify struct layouts, causing storage corruption.
findings.exploit_sketch:
1. Future upgrade adds field to EngineStorage struct
2. Field inserted in wrong position, overwriting existing data
3. All protocol state becomes corrupted
4. Funds locked, operations fail
findings.mitigation: Add storage layout compatibility tests and upgrade simulation tests

findings.title: Library Storage Access Pattern Correct
findings.cwe: CWE-668: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
findings.description: All libraries correctly use the same ENGINE_STORAGE_LOCATION constant as QualityEngine. Storage access is properly isolated via ERC-7201 namespace.
findings.exploit_sketch: N/A - This is a positive finding
findings.impact: N/A - Libraries correctly access shared storage

findings.title: Initialization Pattern Secure
findings.description: Both contracts use proper OpenZeppelin upgradeable patterns: constructor calls _disableInitializers(), initialize functions use initializer modifier.
findings.exploit_sketch: N/A - This is a positive finding

findings.title: Proxy Pattern Standard Compliant
findings.cwe: CWE-668: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
findings.description: Contracts use ERC-1967 proxy standard with UUPS upgradeable pattern. Proxy deployment correctly initializes implementations.
findings.exploit_sketch: N/A - This is a positive finding
findings.impact: N/A - Proxy pattern implementation is correct
findings.mitigation: N/A - Current implementation follows best practices

findings.title: Consensus Algorithm Pluggability Unused
findings.cwe: CWE-710: Improper Adherence to Coding Standards
findings.description: Consensus algorithm address is stored in storage but ConsensusLib.calculate() is called directly instead of via pluggable interface. Limits upgrade flexibility.
findings.exploit_sketch: Future consensus algorithm upgrades require code changes instead of just updating the stored address.
findings.impact: Reduced upgrade flexibility for consensus changes

findings.title: ReentrancyGuard Import Inconsistency
findings.cwe: CWE-710: Improper Adherence to Coding Standards
findings.description: QualityEngine imports non-upgradeable ReentrancyGuard instead of ReentrancyGuardUpgradeable. Functions correctly due to EIP-1153 transient storage in OZ v5.
findings.exploit_sketch: N/A - OZ v5 uses transient storage, making this functionally safe
findings.impact: Minor best practice violation, functionally correct
